turns.question: Should a customer-facing reporting API query Snowflake directly or serve precomputed reporting data from Postgres?
turns.objective: Find out: Should a customer-facing reporting API query Snowflake directly or serve precomputed reporting data from Postgres
turns.config: searchBudget=6 spendLimit=500¢ stages=[GATHER, FILL_GAPS] outputTokens=8000 wordingCheck=false
turns.shown:
Snowflake direct vs precomputed Postgres for a reporting API — Not established: no source supported what this rests on.
No source states a single correct answer, because this is a design trade-off. Given your constraint to serve from Postgres, the evidence supports that choice, with a caveat about newer Snowflake options. Only indicated, not established: - Standard warehouses: The default maximum concurrency on a Snowflake warehouse is 8 queries. Only indicated, not established: One secondary source says queries beyond that limit are queued. That is a poor fit for many simultaneous customer requests unless you add warehouses or clusters. [1] [3] [20] [2] - Newer Snowflake option: Snowflake made interactive tables and interactive warehouses generally available on Dec 11, 2025 (the cited sources do not show: Newer Snowflake). Only indicated, not established: It describes them as delivering low-latency performance for high-concurrency workloads such as data-powered APIs. So "Snowflake can't serve an API" is no longer a safe assumption. I did not find independent benchmarks or cost comparisons. [4] I found no source on the Snowflake-to-Postgres load step, which you would have to build. Rests on findings that are not established: - Pick: Precomputing into Postgres is the sensible choice given your constraint.
Caveat: Only indicated, not established: A standard Snowflake warehouse defaults to a maximum concurrency level of 8, and queries beyond its capacity are queued.
Caveat: Only indicated, not established: Snowflake's interactive tables and interactive warehouses have been generally available since Dec 11, 2025. Snowflake positions them for low-latency, high-concurrency workloads such as data-powered APIs.
Caveat: Only indicated, not established: Under the stated constraint, serve precomputed reporting data from Postgres and refresh it from Snowflake on a schedule. Assumes: Reports are predictable, such as fixed aggregates per customer. Data a few minutes or hours old is acceptable. Changes if: Customers need ad hoc queries over large or fresh data. In that case, benchmark Snowflake interactive warehouses (c2) against your load.

What I couldn't establish
- Latency and cost of Snowflake interactive warehouses versus a Postgres read path — I searched Snowflake's own material and found vendor claims, but no independent benchmark I could use.
- Best method to sync precomputed results from Snowflake into Postgres — my searches did not surface an authoritative source on this.
- When the c1 default was set — The documentation page is the primary source for the default of 8. Its search copy shows no date, and the search tool reports its age as about 1,300 days. A re-check on the live parameter reference page is still needed to confirm it is current. Other pages, including a 2026 tuning guide, also say th
- c2 currency — I found no new evidence this round. The held release note carries its own date, 2025-12-11. I did not look for any later change to the interactive tables feature.
